slot_generation_prompt: Select a complete legal 27-slot genome. Preserve diversity across economy, construction, production, army composition, attack timing, target ranking, rallying, fallback, and defense dimensions; every value must use the declared finite domain.

report.architecture_summary: A deterministic, complete CandidateAgent scaffold exposes a 27-slot strategy grammar. Evolution can recombine economy, construction, production, combat composition, attack timing, target ranking, rallying, fallbacks, and defense without generating arbitrary Java.
decision_flow: Observe the active player, units, resources, and immutable UnitTypeTable through the fixed AgentContext.
Choose construction placement, worker reserve, resource assignment, and worker fallback from finite controls.
Schedule Barracks construction, worker expansion, and combat production under a recombinable priority and expansion mode.
Gate combat on an attack trigger, choose rally behavior, and issue bounded attack orders.
Rank enemy targets, optionally focus fire, choose attack order and distance policy, then use safe command helpers.
Apply the optional in-range defense fallback and translate abstract actions.
invariants: Only active-player units may issue actions through the fixed helper API.
All construction positions are map-bounded and require a free adjacent cell.
All production choices are restricted to Worker, Light, Heavy, or Ranged UnitTypes supported by the scaffold.
Target selection can only choose observed enemy units; no arbitrary Java or runtime LLM path exists.
Every control is finite, run-frozen, and rendered deterministically into the editable strategy region.

assumptions: The standard MicroRTS UnitTypeTable contains Resource, Worker, Light, Heavy, Ranged, Base, and Barracks types.
The checked-in CandidateAgent scaffold and its action helpers are the authoritative compile and safety contract.
Adjacent Barracks construction is sufficient to explore early and delayed production strategies across the configured maps.
risks: Some recombinations intentionally choose slow or non-producing plans; evaluation and EA selection must discard them.
Heavy and Ranged production can be resource-sensitive on small maps, so the genome keeps explicit worker and reserve controls.
Rally and in-range-only combinations may delay attacks but create useful complementary behaviors for EA to select and cross.
